# ISO 8583 Testbed Simulation Results

**Generated by:** `scripts/iso8583-testbed-simulation.py`  
**Paper:** Adaptive DDoS Defense Strategies for High-Throughput Payment Processing Systems  
**Section:** IX.C.1 — TAADA Testbed Validation  
**Date:** 2026-03-18

## Simulation Configuration

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Hardware | Apple M-series ARM64 (simulation only; no live K8s cluster) |
| Random seed | 42 |
| Samples per scenario | 5,000 latency draws |
| Transaction SLA | 50.0 ms (processor-internal authorization segment) |
| Network base latency | 8 ms + N(0, 2ms) jitter |
| Transaction mix | Authorization 85%, Reversal 10%, Balance Inquiry 5% |
| Attack types | SYN Flood (L3/L4), Authorization API Flood (L7), BIN Enumeration |
| Intensities | Light, Moderate, Heavy |
| TPS levels | Baseline 1K, Peak 10K, Stress 50K |
| Total scenarios | 27 (3 × 3 × 3) |

## Key Findings

- **SLA improvement:** TAADA raises mean SLA compliance from 70.7% to 100.0% across all 27 scenarios (3 attack types × 3 intensities × 3 TPS tiers).
- **Latency reduction:** TAADA defense activation reduces mean P99 latency by 22.5 ms on average, with larger reductions at heavy attack intensity where without-TAADA latency is most elevated.
- **Delta_budget adherence:** 100% of scenarios maintain Delta_budget > 0 after TAADA defense deployment (minimum observed: 24.15 ms). All defense bundles fit within the T_SLA = 50 ms constraint.
- **Detection latency:** TAADA mean time-to-respond is 1656 ms (detection + classification + activation). BIN Enumeration has the highest detection latency (2885 ms) due to the slower entropy accumulation signal; SYN Flood detection is fastest.
- **Residual attack traffic:** SYN Flood bundles (BGP Flowspec + SYN Cookies + eBPF/XDP) achieve the highest combined effectiveness (>95% attack rejection at heavy intensity); Auth API Flood with WAF addition reaches ~97% effectiveness at heavy intensity.

## Comparison with Section IX.C.1 (Original TAADA Simulation)

The original TAADA simulation (`scripts/taada-simulation.py`) validated Delta_budget adherence across all 24 experiment scenarios (T1-T24) at three TPS tiers using the defense budget equation. Key comparisons:

| Metric | Original Simulation | ISO 8583 Testbed |
|--------|--------------------|-----------------------|
| SLA compliance | 100% (72/72 scenarios) | 100.0% (27/27 scenarios) |
| Mean Delta_budget | Varies by tier (see taada-simulation.py output) | 28.79 ms |
| Detection latency modeled | Not modeled (budget-equation only) | 1656 ms mean |
| Traffic model | Abstract (no packet-level simulation) | ISO 8583 Poisson arrivals, time-of-day variation |
| Attack injection | Multiplier-based residual model | Explicit rate-based degradation curves |

**Alignment:** The ISO 8583 testbed simulation confirms the original TAADA finding that all defense bundles maintain Delta_budget > 0 across attack types and intensities. The defense overhead values are consistent between simulations (drawn from the same DEFENSE_CATALOG). The ISO 8583 simulation adds time-resolved traffic modeling and explicit detection latency, showing TAADA can respond within ~1,000-3,800 ms of attack onset across the three attack types — a result not captured in the original budget-equation simulation.

**Differences:** The ISO 8583 testbed uses a fixed T_baseline of ~20ms (weighted average of transaction processing + network latency), while the original simulation uses tier-specific baselines (28ms for 50K+). This produces slightly different Delta_budget values but does not change compliance outcomes. The testbed also models TPS degradation via explicit throughput curves rather than the multiplicative residual model in taada-simulation.py, resulting in more conservative (lower) TPS maintained estimates under heavy attacks.
